name: Call of Earth

angles.text: This rite marks a pivotal threshold in a shaman's training, where commune with the earth grants strength, stamina, and deep spiritual insight.
Reverence for the Earth Mother is central to tauren culture, making this trial an observance of fundamental ancestral beliefs.
The shamanic traditions that bind the Horde draw upon the elements, beginning with the grounded resilience of the earth.

faq.answer: Call of Earth is a sacred spiritual trial for an aspiring shaman. It tests a seeker's patience and readiness to commune directly with the element of earth and heed its eternal wisdom.
faq.q: What is the Call of Earth?

faq.answer: Earth represents the foundation of all things, embodying strength, stamina, and patience. Considered the most stubborn and wise of the elements, it teaches that all things erode and are reborn across time.
faq.q: What does the earth element represent in shamanic tradition?

faq.answer: A sapta is an elemental draught prepared by a shaman mentor. Drinking or accepting it opens a spiritual path, attuning the seeker's senses to perceive and interact with elemental spirits.

The Earth Mother is the foundational source of life and balance revered especially by tauren shamans. She protects those who honor her laws and grants greater wisdom to seekers who treat the land with respect.
faq.q: Who is the Earth Mother mentioned in the trial?

aliases: what happens when you complete it
faq.answer: Completing this stage signifies that the seeker is prepared for the next step of their path. It represents a spiritual rebirth from which a shaman can never return to ignorance, as new secrets of the earth are unveiled.
faq.q: What happens upon answering the call?

faq.answer: The earth operates on cycles of erosion and rebirth where mountains eventually wear into deserts and rivers carve canyons. A shaman must master patience and stamina to attune to such enduring rhythms.
faq.q: Why is patience required to commune with the earth?

sections.body: The Call of Earth is a formative rite for a shaman learning to commune with the primal forces of the world. Earth is regarded as the most stubborn and wise of all elements, serving as the steady bedrock of existence. The trial emphasizes that nature moves in deliberate cycles of erosion and rebirth, transforming mountains into deserts and rivers into canyons over countless ages. To hear the voice of the earth, an initiate must embody that same unwavering patience.
sections.title: The Foundation of All Things

sections.body: Answering this call is considered a spiritual rebirth that leaves the seeker irrevocably altered, unable to return to their former ignorance. Upon proving their readiness and respect for the laws of the Earth Mother, the initiate is granted an earthen sapta. This specialized elixir opens a new path of perception, enabling the shaman to grasp the foundational secrets of strength, stamina, and elemental protection.
sections.title: The Sapta and Rebirth

summary: Call of Earth is a sacred shamanic rite of passage that tests an initiate's patience, endurance, and respect for the natural world. By answering the earth's call and accepting the elemental sapta, the seeker embarks on a spiritual rebirth to commune directly with the foundation of all life.
